note: Single source of truth for the Grade Board tune maths. Every constant the grade uses lives HERE and
nowhere else. grade_math.py reads this file at import; grade_math.js reads it via init(); the GLSL the
page compiles is GENERATED by grade_math.js from these same numbers, so the shader physically cannot
run a different constant from the bake. selftest_math.py proves the Python and the JavaScript agree to
better than 1e-5 on 200 random colours - run it after any edit to this file.
Two implementations of one maths is the way this board fails: you grade one thing and ship another.
The rule is: change a number here, run the selftest, and the drift is impossible.

formulas.exposure: c = c * pow(2, exposure)   -- stops, 0 = identity
formulas.levels: c = (c - black) / max(white - black, levels_eps)   -- black defaults to the measured 0.5th pct luma, white to the 99.5th; a black BELOW the measured point lifts the shadows, above it crushes them
formulas.clamp: c = clamp(c, 0, 1)   -- HSV is undefined outside the unit cube and the LUT domain is [0,1], so the clamp is part of the maths, not a guard
skin_rotate: w = 1 - t*t*(3 - 2*t)            -- soft falloff: 1 on the skin hue, 0 at the band edge, flat at both ends

pre_pass.why_hue_selective: A global hue shift that fixed the skin dragged the backdrop purple. The +/-35 deg band with a soft falloff moves the face and leaves the wall. Greys need no gate - at s=0 the rotation is a no-op by construction.

formulas.mix: c = c + (lut(c) - c) * mix   -- lerp identity -> LUT; mix 1 is the LUT at full strength
formulas.temp: c.r += temp * temp_r ; c.b -= temp * temp_b
formulas.tint: c.g += tint * tint_g ; c.r -= tint * tint_rb ; c.b -= tint * tint_rb
formulas.saturation: l = dot(c, luma) ; c = l + (c - l) * (1 + sat * sat_gain)
formulas.matte: m = mat * matte_max ; c = c * (1 - m) + m   -- lifts the floor, never touches white

slot.stacking: Slots run in order, 1..5. Slot 2 grades slot 1's output, not the raw. Five 3D lookups per pixel is free; the cap is UI, not maths.

ranges_note: [min, max, step, default] - the sliders on the page are built from this table, so a range change is also one edit in one file.
